rationale: All three lenses ran (blind, edge-case, acceptance) and the acceptance lens passed every ticket and plan criterion. Triage dropped 14 unique concerns after merging duplicates: the substantive ones were verified against the code and found inapplicable (a subagent's Agent call and its result live in the same transcript, `ContentBlock` is still used, ids are unique per call, the live path only counts a call after its result exists except on the final pass, and the OTLP summary is a full snapshot so nothing needs retracting) or follow repo convention (`=== true` flag check). One defer: a denied/errored `Skill` call is still over-counted in `skills`, a pre-existing flaw left out of scope by decision and worth its own ticket. Two points to weigh, neither blocking: (1) any `is_error` result is excluded, so an agent that started and then errored or was interrupted is also not counted; this is what the ticket's stated fix asks for ('not denied/error') and no positive 'started' signal is available to separate the cases; (2) the repo has no real transcript of a hook-denied Agent call, so 'denial gives is_error:true' rests on QA comment 3 and is encoded only in the test fixture.
